title: Generative AI enables medical image segmentation in ultra low-data regimes (GenSeg)
mechanism: Pixel-space mask-to-image GAN fed with augmented real masks; generator architecture learned by multi-level optimisation so the segmenter's validation loss steers generation.
adaptation: Pixel space keeps cracks. Train on 478 cells at 512 px or 256 crops; mask augmentations = flips, rot90, crack evolution, inactive region edits; validation = module-grouped CV fold or F51, never test. Snap crack labels to the ridge first. Target inactive and weak sources (BMRK, CFVS without twin).
min_experiment: PF + GenSeg pairs (2x train size) vs PF, 5 seeds. Metric CV inactive IoU, BMRK crack/inactive IoU, mIoU_rob. Kill: CV inactive < +0.02 and mIoU_rob < +0.01. About 36 GPU-h.
evidence: R: 11 tasks, 19 datasets, 8 to 480 training images per task, +10 to 20% absolute Dice/IoU in- and out-of-domain; 8 to 20x less data needed. Code stated as github importZL/semantic_segmentation (not opened).
